findings.evidence: Line 161-163 `isOneLoopRGSolution_oneLoopCoupling ... IsOneLoopRGSolution β₀ {t | 1 + β₀ * a₀ * t ≠ 0}`; line 252-254 concludes only `t₀ + landauTime β₀ (f t₀) ∉ Ioo A B`.
findings.fix: Reword to "...at the finite time `landauTime β₀ a₀ = -(β₀ a₀)⁻¹`, through which no solution of the truncated equation continues".
findings.issue: Module docstring says the coupling blows up at `landauTime β₀ a₀` "below which no solution extends at all". That is false: solutions exist entirely below the Landau time — `isOneLoopRGSolution_oneLoopCoupling β₀ a₀` holds on `{t | 1 + β₀ a₀ t ≠ 0}`, which contains all `t < landauTime β₀ a₀` (there `1 + β₀ a₀ t < 0`). What `add_landauTime_notMem` proves is that no solution's interval *contains* its own Landau time.

findings.evidence: Statement at lines 252-254 is a non-membership claim about `Ioo A B` for the given `f`, not a non-existence claim about the equation at that time.
findings.fix: Drop the clause, or replace with "so a solution's domain stops short of its own Landau time". The first sentence of the docstring is already accurate.
findings.issue: Docstring of `IsOneLoopRGSolution.add_landauTime_notMem` adds "the truncated equation has no solution there". The equation does have solutions at that point (through any nonzero value, by `isOneLoopRGSolution_oneLoopCoupling` re-referenced there); what fails is that *this* solution's interval cannot reach it.

findings.evidence: Line 141 `def IsOneLoopRGSolution (β₀ : ℝ) (s : Set ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ)`; line 237-239 `eq_oneLoopCoupling` hypotheses `IsOneLoopRGSolution β₀ (Ioo A B) f`, `ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ioo A B`, `h₀ : f t₀ ≠ 0`.
findings.fix: Qualify both: "on an open interval, a solution that is nonzero at one point of the interval is a one-loop coupling (`IsOneLoopRGSolution.eq_oneLoopCoupling`)".
findings.issue: `IsOneLoopRGSolution` is defined for an arbitrary set `s`, but its docstring claims "The solutions are exactly the one-loop couplings of `oneLoopCoupling`". `eq_oneLoopCoupling` only gives this for `s = Ioo A B` and `f` nonzero at a point; on a disconnected `s` (e.g. `Ioo 0 1 ∪ Ioo 2 3` with different `a₀` on each piece) the predicate holds for functions that are no single `oneLoopCoupling`. Same unqualified claim in the module docstring, line 29-30 ("it is the only one through a nonzero initial value").

summary: The module docstring and the Landau-pole theorem's docstring overclaim what is proved about non-continuation past the Landau time, and the `IsOneLoopRGSolution` docstring asserts an exact characterisation of solutions that only holds on an open interval. Everything else (definitions, main theorems, the `SU(N_c)` window, the `oneLoopAlphaS` distinction, references) is documented accurately.
